name: SpookySwap
rootCause: DEX SpookySwap on Fantom tweeted that the team is investigating a frontend vulnerability on their domain. Please do not execute any transactions on the DEX. On November 19, Spooky updated that a 3rd party JavaScript plugin enabled code injection from npm packages. This enabled replacing the spooky router contract on the Spooky Fi frontend with a malicious contract which sent funds that users attempted to swap to the exploiter.

descriptions.text: DEX SpookySwap on Fantom tweeted that the team is investigating a frontend vulnerability on their domain. Please do not execute any transactions on the DEX. On November 19, Spooky updated that a 3rd party JavaScript plugin enabled code injection from npm packages. This enabled replacing the spooky router contract on the Spooky Fi frontend with a malicious contract which sent funds that users attempted to swap to the exploiter.

On November 18, 2023, the SpookySwap decentralized exchange on Fantom suffered a $5,000 loss after attackers compromised its web frontend. Users interacting with the site during the incident were misdirected to attacker-controlled wallets, leading to theft of funds. Backend smart contracts were not affected, and the frontend was relaunched after remediation. The attack was enabled by compromise of SpookySwap’s web frontend, allowing malicious scripts or redirects to reroute user transactions to addresses controlled by the attacker. The technical entry point (such as DNS, hosting, or repository compromise) was not publicly disclosed.
